findings.reason: a worker following §3 would revive dead code believing it is the sanctioned creation path, instead of extending the function actually doing the work.
findings.text: the plan's §3 prior-art claim ("the existing owner of SignalSource creation, create_signal_source") is checked by opening the code: `grep -rn create_signal_source` across imas_codex/ and tests/ returns only the definition at grouping.py:26 and the docstring at grouping.py:9 — no caller. The mechanism the plan cites as existing does not exist in the live call graph

findings.reason: without naming the live owner, the plan forks a fourth path off a shared mechanism whose two existing creators already disagree, and the signal-group path (parallel.py) is the one the singleton work must live beside.
findings.text: SignalSource creation for FacilitySignals is owned by detect_signal_sources (parallel.py:1556, invoked at parallel.py:5077 preflight and parallel.py:3643 enrich-loop), which builds the node with its own inline `MERGE (sg:SignalSource {id: $group_id}) ON CREATE SET …` rather than calling create_signal_source; §3 proposes a further singleton path through grouping.py:26, leaving the census of creators at three: detect_signal_sources (parallel.py:1556, live, FacilitySignal), detect_and_create_signal_sources (imas_codex/discovery/mdsplus/graph_ops.py:455, live, inline MERGE at graph_ops.py:556, SignalNode), and create_signal_source (grouping.py:26, dead). The owner §3 must extend is parallel.py:1556

findings.reason: the honest change may be to unify the three creators and extend the existing grouping rather than add a parallel routine, which is exactly the reuse question §3 must answer.
findings.text: existing singleton-capable behaviour is not recognised: detect_signal_sources already takes min_instances (parallel.py:1556, default 3) and groups by pattern template, so a signal whose accessor pattern is unique forms a one-member group at min_instances=1; the plan adds a separate "singleton SignalSource" routine for enriched standalones without stating why extending this parameterised grouping (or extracting the inline MERGE at parallel.py:1617-1650 into create_signal_source, unifying all three creators) cannot serve

findings.reason: the section must account for the interface surface it adds in its own text, and here that accounting is the same question as the duplicate-owner reconciliation.
findings.text: §3 adds a new singleton-source creation definition/path (write paths imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py and imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py) with public_definitions at 0 for the week and no sentence naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be; the section should state that it extends the existing creator rather than adds one, or name the surface it removes

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no new module; §3 extends an existing discovery stage, §4 edits the single unit-alias data file, and §8 extends the existing search_dd_paths tool, so no behaviour is spread across shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan routes its new singleton creation through a dead function while the SignalSource-creation family already carries two live, duplicated inline creators it does not reconcile.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 introduces a new singleton-source creation definition/path without naming in its own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 cites create_signal_source (imas_codex/discovery/base/grouping.py:26) as "the existing owner of SignalSource creation", but that function has no callers anywhere in the repository; the live machinery that creates SignalSource for these signals is detect_signal_sources (imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:1556), which the plan names only as a write path without identifying it as the owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no wrapper is proposed; §8 explicitly reuses the search-time rerank owner that discovery-judgments-through-jev §9 lands rather than adding a second rerank, and §4 extends the alias file the registry already loads instead of layering a parser over it.
